title: You didn’t just “share a post.”
paragraphs: You knew where it came from.

You saw the watermark. You recognized the caption wasn’t yours. You felt that small hesitation… and then you posted it anyway, maybe trimmed the credit, maybe removed it completely, maybe said nothing at all.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
And the moment you start preaching truth while living in quiet dishonesty, something fractures inside your witness.
Because Scripture doesn’t just talk about big, obvious sins. It goes straight for the hidden ones we excuse.
No footnote. No exception for “it’s for ministry.” No clause that says “unless it’s about God.”
Stealing isn’t sanctified just because the subject is holy.
If anything, it becomes more serious.
Because now you’re attaching God’s name to something that wasn’t honestly yours.
“Therefore, having put away falsehood, let each one of you speak the truth with his neighbor…” — Ephesians 4:25
Not just lies spoken out loud… but false impressions.
Taking someone else’s words or work and presenting it as your own is a form of falsehood, even if the message itself is biblical.
There’s a tension here most people try to avoid.
They’ll say, “But I’m spreading the Gospel. Isn’t that what matters?”
Because God never needs sin to spread His truth.
“Will you speak falsely for God and speak deceitfully for Him?” — Job 13:7
That question cuts deeper than people expect.
Will you take what isn’t yours… for God?
Will you ignore integrity… for God?
The answer Scripture demands is clear.
Because when you do that, you’re no longer representing Him—you’re using Him.
You might even feel like you’re doing something meaningful.
But inside, something starts to dull.
And before long, you’re not just reposting without credit…
You’re building a version of yourself that isn’t real.
Jesus didn’t just confront obvious sinners.
He confronted religious people who looked right but lived wrong underneath.
“Beware of practicing your righteousness before other people in order to be seen by them…” — Matthew 6:1
That includes the quiet desire to be recognized for something you didn’t actually do.
Yes—if you knowingly take what isn’t yours and present it in a way that misleads, it falls under theft and falsehood.
But don’t miss the deeper issue.
It’s about the condition of your heart.
Are you hungry to be seen…
Because God isn’t impressed by viral posts.
He looks at truth in the inner being.
“Behold, you delight in truth in the inward being…” — Psalm 51:6
And here’s the part most people don’t expect—
This isn’t where the story ends.
If this hit you, if something in you tightened while reading this…
You don’t need to fake impact.
You don’t need to steal words to be used.
You don’t need to build a platform on something fragile.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
You can go back and give credit.
You can choose honesty even if it costs you recognition.
And God will actually be in it.
If you’ve done this, say it plainly—“Lord, I did it.”
Let it be your line in the sand.
Follow this journey if you’re done playing appearances and you want something deeper, something that actually transforms.
You’ll need to read it again the next time temptation whispers, “No one will notice.”
And if you’re ready to grow in truth, correction, and real Gospel depth, step into what’s being built here:
It’s about becoming someone God can trust.
